description: Both sources state a read timeout and they disagree. merged.md surfaces both values instead of picking a winner, which is the rewarded behaviour, but attaches each value to the wrong source document: the Deployment Notes are credited with source_a.md's 30 seconds and the Operator Guide with source_b.md's 60 seconds. Every value survives, so the forward probes are clean and the defect is only reachable from merged.md.
plants: attribution swapped between the two named sources

probes.text: The Deployment Notes state the read timeout is 30 seconds.
probes.note: source_b.md is the Deployment Notes and states 60 seconds, so the merge attributes a value to a document that states a different one. The discriminating span cannot be excluded from merged.md here: merged.md surfaces both 30 and 60 by design.

probes.text: The Operator Guide states the read timeout is 60 seconds.
probes.note: source_a.md is the Operator Guide and states 30 seconds, so this line attributes a value to a document that states a different one -- the other half of the same swap as m-notes-timeout-attribution. Probed separately because a finding on it is a correct reading, and until this probe existed every arm that made it was recorded as having invented a finding.

expected_conflicts.reason: source_a.md states 30 seconds and source_b.md states 60 seconds for the same attribute
expected_conflicts.note: Surfaced by merged.md rather than silently resolved, as in conflict_surfaced. Detecting it is the conflict check's assertion.
